review: T-20 commit d9fa131 (prompt v4, extraction guards, diet facts, eval runner), read-only adversarial workflow, 2026-10-20
method: 4 dimension reviewers (guards, prompt, facts-cases-tests, runner) over git diff 6cfa174..d9fa131; one skeptic per dimension tried to refute each finding (default refuted when uncertain). No files written, no tests or model calls during review.

findings.title: Clock-time guard checks the whole message for any digit or number word, so an invented time still gets through whenever a party size or date is in the same message
findings.scenario: The draft is the SC-REG-006 one (hauz-khas, 2026-10-17, 20:00, dinner, 4). The guest says "actually make it lunch for 2 instead" (or "make it lunch on the 18th instead", "lunch instead, same four of us"). The model makes the same mistake as LV-CONF-001 in v4-try1 and returns time "12:00", timeWindow "lunch". CLOCK_RE matches the "2", so the guard keeps the time. mergeExtracted then passes statedTime=true to latestWins, so 12:00 survives, selected is cleared, and availabilityStep finds an exact 12:00 slot (LV-CONF-001 shows 12:00 open). The guest gets a confirm card for 12:00 PM, a time they never gave. The same applies to first messages like "Can I book for two this Sunday evening at the Gurugram one?" (both "two" and "one" match) or "for 3 on 2 November, evening" if the model invents 19:00.
findings.evidence: `const CLOCK_RE = /\p{Nd}|\b(?:noon|midday|midnight|half|quarter|one|two|...|twelve)\b/iu;` and in turn.ts:209 `if (turn.booking.time !== null && !statesClockTime(latest))`. The test is 'does any digit or number word appear anywhere in the message', not 'is there a clock time'. Party sizes ("2", "two of us", "one of us"), dates ("18th", "2 November", "17-10-2026") and phrases like "the Gurugram one" all pass it. Nearly every real booking message has a party size, so the guard only covers follow-ups with no numbers at all, which is the one shape SC-REG-006 tests. router.ts:165-168 then turns any exact match into a confirm block.

findings.title: A real time is dropped when written as a number word with a suffix ('nineish', 'eightish') or as 'nineteen hundred'; the old time's confirm card then comes back as if the change worked
findings.scenario: A confirm card is showing for hauz-khas 2026-10-17 20:00, 4 guests (timeWindow null). The guest asks "can we do nineish instead?" and the model returns time "21:00". \bnine\b does not match inside "nineish" because there is no word boundary before "ish", and no other token matches, so turn.ts drops the time and records ignore_field. mergeExtracted then sees all nulls: nothing changes and withSelection keeps the selection. nextStep goes to availabilityStep, which finds the exact 20:00 slot and shows the confirm card for 8:00 PM again with "Here are your booking details... tap Confirm". The guest asked for about 9 PM and gets the 8 PM card. "sevenish", "eightish", "nineteen hundred" and "twenty hundred hours" fail the same way. With no earlier time, the guest is shown all slots instead.
findings.evidence: The number-word branch is `\b(?:...|seven|eight|nine|...)\b`, which requires a boundary after the word. The unit test (chat-draft.test.ts:87) only checks "around seven", "half past seven" and similar, and has no '-ish' or compound forms. After the drop, `latestWins(draft, next, booking.time !== null, rejected)` gets statedTime=false with no window change, so the old draft.time is kept (null never clears) and router.ts:165 `const exact = draft.time ? r.slots.find((s) => s.time === draft.time)` produces the confirm card.

findings.title: When exactly one ambiguity reading is usable, the older draft value is kept and its confirm card is shown again; the new comment says the flow 'asks plainly', which is only true for an empty field
findings.scenario: A confirm card is showing for 4 guests at 20:00 tomorrow. The guest says "actually there might be 8 or 9 of us". The model returns partySize null with ambiguity {field: partySize, candidates: ["8","9"]}. "9" is large_party, so candidates is ["8"] (length 1): ambiguity stays null, and unusable stays null because candidates.length !== 0. The loop skips the null partySize, so nothing changes and the selection is kept. nextStep then calls availabilityStep with partySize 4 and shows the 4-guest confirm card again. By contrast, "9 or 10" gets the large-party redirect. The same thing happens for a date ambiguity where one reading is past the horizon: the old date's card comes back.
findings.evidence: `if (candidates.length >= 2) ambiguity = ...;` `// With exactly one usable reading the flow asks plainly rather than guessing.` `if (candidates.length === 0 && first && !first.ok) unusable = ...`. The field is cleared only on the 0-usable path, through issues → rejected → latestWins. The test that covers this case uses `draft({})` (chat-draft.test.ts:72, "one usable: ask plainly"), so it never checks a draft that already has a value. This goes against §5.7: 'The latest stated value wins' and 'If one message contradicts itself, ask'. The behaviour was there before this commit, but the new branch and its comment describe it as handled.

findings.title: Tests for both guards only cover number-free messages and empty drafts, so the gaps above would go unnoticed
findings.scenario: If the model invents 12:00 for "make it lunch for 2 instead", or 19:00 for "Can I book for two this Sunday evening at the Gurugram one?", every test still passes. The unit negatives ("actually make it lunch instead", "can we switch to dinner?", ...) contain no digit or number word. SC-REG-006 uses the same number-free message. The live cases with a meal or part of the day plus numbers (LV-BK-001, LV-BK-009, LV-REG-009) check draft fields without time and have no noActions:["confirm"]. An invented-time confirm card would pass all of them.
findings.evidence: chat-draft.test.ts:89-90 negatives are all number-free. scripted-regressions.jsonl SC-REG-006 turn: "actually make it lunch instead". live-d2.jsonl:19 LV-BK-001 expect `{"draft": {"branch": "gurugram", "date": "2026-10-18", "timeWindow": "dinner", "partySize": 2}}` (no time:null, no noActions). live-d2.jsonl:27 LV-BK-009 and live-regressions.jsonl:9 LV-REG-009 are the same. No test asserts that the guard keeps a time written as a compound word or with '-ish'.

findings.title: The unusable-ambiguity reason comes from whichever candidate is listed first, so the guest can be given the wrong reason
findings.scenario: Today is Fri 16 Oct 2026. The guest asks for "30 December" and the model returns ambiguity date candidates ["2025-12-30", "2026-12-30"]. Both fail, and checked[0] is past_date, so the guest hears "That date has passed. Which date would you like?" The real reason is the 30-day limit (pastHorizon), which SC-REG-005 expects only because its candidates happen to be listed upcoming year first. For mixed partySize candidates such as ["0","12"], the guest gets a plain 'How many guests?' instead of the large-party phone template.
findings.evidence: `const first = checked[0]; if (candidates.length === 0 && first && !first.ok) unusable = { field, issue: first.issue };`. The code does not rank issues (for example preferring past_horizon or large_party over past_date or bad_party). router.ts ISSUE_TEXT maps past_date to T.pastDate.

findings.title: The not-stated guard only drops booking.time; a time ambiguity from a message with no time still produces time chips
findings.scenario: The guest says "actually make it lunch instead". The model sets time null but returns ambiguity {field: "time", candidates: ["12:00","13:00"]}. The guard looks only at turn.booking.time, so mergeExtracted builds an ambiguity, and nextStep replies "Which time did you mean?" with 12:00 PM / 1:00 PM chips. Those are times the guest never mentioned, offered without an availability check. Tapping one goes through applySetField to a confirm card if the slot is open.
findings.evidence: `if (turn.booking.time !== null && !statesClockTime(latest)) { ... turn = { ...turn, booking: { ...turn.booking, time: null } }; }` leaves booking.ambiguity alone. draft.ts:83 `if (candidates.length >= 2) ambiguity = { field, candidates };` accepts field "time", and router.ts:115-119 turns it into fieldChips("time", ctx, candidates).

findings.title: gitSha, gitDirty and the dataset hash are read when the run ends, not when its code and cases were loaded, so a commit or edit during a background run gets attached to a run that never used it
findings.scenario: verify:release starts at commit A on a clean tree. tsx loads every lib/ module and loadCases() reads evals/cases at startup (L549). During the 13+ minute `eval --runs 3` step, the agent commits T-20 (2/2) as commit B. Under §6.6 that commit adds a regression case to evals/cases/live-regressions.jsonl. At the end, meta records gitSha=B and gitDirty=false, and dataset.hash covers B's case files while dataset.cases still counts A's 91 cases. The committed results file then says B passed the release D2 run, but B's code and its new case were never run. The reverse also happens. The tree is clean when the run starts, and the agent then edits docs/STATUS.md or creates docs/EVAL_REPORT.md while the run is in the background (as §6.1 and CLAUDE.md direct). The run that used committed code is then saved with gitDirty=true.
findings.evidence: L617 `gitSha: sh("git", ["rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"])` and L619 `gitDirty: (sh("git", ["status", "--porcelain"]) ?? "")...` are both inside `const meta = {...}`, which is built after the run loop (L583-590), measureRetrieval and ollamaState. The dataset hash is computed the same way at L610-613: `fs.readdirSync(casesDir)...readFileSync` re-reads the case files from disk at the end. `cases` itself was loaded at L549. All lib code is imported statically, so it is fixed at process start. The new comment says the field shows whether 'gitSha alone does not identify the code that ran', but the value describes the tree at the end of the run, not at the start. The fix is to record sha, dirty and hash before the first case (and optionally again at the end, saving both).

findings.title: gitDirty reports a clean tree when git fails, and the substring filter can hide changed code
findings.scenario: (a) The runner is started from outside the repo, e.g. `node --import tsx "/…/Restraunt Chatbot/evals/run.ts" --mode live` from $HOME. `sh` runs git in process.cwd(), not ROOT, so both git calls fail and return null. The result says gitSha:null, gitDirty:false, i.e. 'clean', when nothing was checked. The same happens when execFileSync throws for any other reason. (b) A staged move such as `git mv lib/chat/draft.ts evals/results/draft.ts` produces the porcelain line `R  lib/chat/draft.ts -> evals/results/draft.ts`. `includes("evals/results/")` drops that line, so gitDirty=false even though lib/chat/draft.ts is gone from the committed code. (c) With `status.showUntrackedFiles=no` in the user's git config, a new untracked source file under lib/ is not listed and gitDirty=false.
findings.evidence: `function sh(...) { try { return execFileSync(cmd, args, { encoding: "utf8", stdio: [...] }).trim(); } catch { return null; } }` has no `cwd: ROOT`. `gitDirty: (sh("git", ["status", "--porcelain"]) ?? "").split("\n").some((l) => l.trim() && !l.includes("evals/results/"))`: a null from sh becomes "" and then false instead of null (unknown). The filter is a substring match on the whole porcelain line (both sides of `->`), not a check on the path prefix. `--untracked-files=normal` is not forced. The runner's own *.partial.jsonl is fine: .gitignore has `evals/results/*.partial.jsonl`, and porcelain does not list it.

findings.title: ollamaState matches models by exact name, so an untagged model reports digest null and 'not loaded' although it served every turn
findings.scenario: lib/config accepts CHAT_MODEL or EMBED_MODEL without a tag (modelName is only `z.string().min(1)` plus a cloud check), e.g. `EMBED_MODEL=qwen3-embedding` or `CHAT_MODEL=Qwen3.5:9B`. Ollama resolves these to `qwen3-embedding:latest` / `qwen3.5:9b`, and /api/tags and /api/ps list them under those names. `m.name === name || m.model === name` never matches, so meta.ollama.models[i] has digest:null and loaded:false, and the console prints `qwen3-embedding ? not loaded`. The §6.6 model digest and the §6.5 `ollama ps` size and GPU share are then missing for a model that ran the whole time. Separately, the digest comes from /api/tags rather than the loaded instance's /api/ps `digest`. If the tag is re-pulled during a run, the result records the new manifest's digest while the old weights were the ones loaded and measured.
findings.evidence: L511 `const find = (list, name) => list?.models?.find((m) => m.name === name || m.model === name);`. L518 `digest: find(tags, name)?.digest?.slice(0, 12) ?? null` is taken from tags even when `p` (the ps entry, which also carries `digest`) exists. L566 passes `names: [config.chatModel, config.embedModel]` exactly as configured, without normalising `:latest`, case or a registry prefix. With the default names (`qwen3.5:9b`, `qwen3-embedding:0.6b`) matching works: the 10-21-07 release result shows digests d63f830f28d5 and ac6da0dfba84. gpuShare when size_vram is missing is not a real issue, because Ollama 0.40.5 always sends size_vram (the results show it).

findings.title: Category lists label vegan dishes only as "vegan"; with v4 rule 4, answers to "which X are vegetarian" now drop every vegan dish
findings.scenario: Guest asks "Which small plates are vegetarian?" (fixture: Kale Pakoda [vegan], Beetroot & Peanut Tikki [vegan], Papdi Chaat, Dahi Puri Shots, Mushroom Galouti). Shown answer in every v4 run (v4-try1, try2, try3, and all 3 runs of 2026-10-20T10-21-07-607Z at d9fa131): "The vegetarian small plates are Papdi Chaat (₹315), Dahi Puri Shots (₹325), and Mushroom Galouti (₹425)." Both vegan plates are missing, so the answer wrongly implies they are not vegetarian. The pre-v4 run (2026-10-20T09-41-21-550Z_qwen3.5-9b_pre-v4.json, at 6cfa174 with no diets in the lists) listed all five. The same applies to mains (Yellow Dal Tadka, Chana Pindi, Baingan Bharta), breads, desserts and drinks.
findings.evidence: `dietText` picks one label: `d.includes("vegan") ? "Vegan" : d.includes("vegetarian") ? "Vegetarian" : "Non-vegetarian"` (line 107). The new `diet(m)` puts that label into each menu-cat entry: `Kale Pakoda ₹295 (vegan, gluten-free); Papdi Chaat ₹315 (vegetarian; contains dairy)`. v4 rule 4 (lib/llm/prompt.ts) adds: "Call a dish vegan, vegetarian ... only if the facts say so for that dish." No menu-cat or per-item fact ever calls a vegan dish "vegetarian". Only menu-diet:vegetarian says "Vegetarian, including vegan", and it was not retrieved. So the model, following its rules, filters on the literal word. Grounding and INV-05 can't catch this: the diet text adds no digits, times, prices, number words or booking-state words. I checked the rest and it is unaffected: indexText for menu-cat is unchanged (lib/kb/index.ts indexes `indexedText`), so retrieval is unchanged. The largest two-aggregate pair is still menu-diet:vegetarian + menu-diet:gluten-free (2453 chars; the largest menu-cat after the change is mains at 646). The worst-case prompt stays about 19k characters, under PROMPT_CHAR_BUDGET 22272.

findings.title: statesClockTime treats any digit or number word as a clock time, so party sizes and dates let an invented time through to a confirm card
findings.scenario: Draft: hauz-khas, 2026-10-17, 20:00, dinner, 4. Guest: "actually make it lunch for 4 instead" (or "lunch on the 18th instead"). The model returns time "12:00", the exact D2 v4-try1 LV-CONF-001 failure. `statesClockTime` matches the "4", so the turn.ts guard keeps the time. `latestWins` gets statedTime=true, so the draft gets time 12:00. That slot is open (Sat lunch 12:00–15:30, T3/T4/T5 free), so a confirm card for 12:00 is shown, a time the guest never gave. SC-REG-006, which is marked critical, only tests the digit-free phrasing. The unit tests' false cases are all digit-free, so nothing catches this.
findings.evidence: `const CLOCK_RE = /\p{Nd}|\b(?:noon|midday|midnight|half|quarter|one|two|three|four|...|twelve)\b/iu;` matches "5 of us", "for four", "the 3rd" and "25 December". turn.ts: `if (turn.booking.time !== null && !statesClockTime(latest)) { ...time: null }` is skipped whenever the message contains any such token. The committed LV cases that contain digits or number words (LV-REG-001 "5 of us", LV-REG-009 "four") therefore get no protection from the guard.

findings.title: LV-REG-005/006 check only for forbidden dish names, so wrong or incomplete diet answers pass and count as grounded-correct
findings.scenario: LV-REG-005 passed in every v4 run with the incomplete answer above, which leaves out Kale Pakoda and Beetroot & Peanut Tikki. Its only checks are intent, "answer" (did not abstain) and four replyMustNotMatch patterns. A reply of "None of our drinks are vegan" would also pass LV-REG-006. The opposite also happens: a correct answer such as "Kokum Cooler and Fresh Lime Soda are vegan; the lassi, chaas, coffee and chai contain dairy" fails, because the patterns are case-insensitive (`new RegExp(re, "i")`). The same goes for "...; the Chicken 65 and Fish Fry are not" in LV-REG-005.
findings.evidence: LV-REG-005: `"expect": {"intent": "faq", "mustAbstain": false, "replyMustNotMatch": ["Fish", "Chicken", "Prawn", "Keema"]}`. LV-REG-006: `"replyMustNotMatch": ["Lassi", "Chaas", "Coffee", "Chai"]`. The case they rephrase, LV-SMOKE-04, also requires `replyMustMatch: ["Mango Sorbet"]` and `mustIncludeValues: ["₹245"]`. §6.2 menu core assertion: "Dish and price match the table". evals/metrics.ts counts the "answer" key in GROUNDED_KEYS, so the incomplete answer raises groundedAnswerCorrectness. With no positive check, such as all five vegetarian small plates or both vegan drinks plus mustCiteAny, the regression in the first finding is invisible to D2.

findings.title: LV-REG-009 does not require time:null, so an invented "night" time would pass (the guard is bypassed by "four")
findings.scenario: Guest: "Can we book for four this Saturday night at Hauz Khas?". If the model returns time "20:00" for "night", statesClockTime returns true (it matches "four"), so the time is kept. The draft becomes {hauz-khas, 2026-10-17, 20:00, dinner, 4} and a confirm card for 8 PM is shown. deepMatch only compares the keys listed, so the case still passes. Per §5.7 and v4 rule 2 ("time ... only if the guest gives a clock time"), time must be null here.
findings.evidence: `"expect": {"intent": "booking", "draft": {"branch": "hauz-khas", "date": "2026-10-17", "timeWindow": "dinner", "partySize": 4}}`: no `"time": null` and no `noActions: ["confirm"]`. evals/run.ts `deepMatch` is a subset match, and the "draft" key feeds bookingFieldExtractionExact ("all fields exact"). The current runs pass for the right reason (slots shown, time null), but the case would not catch an invented time.

findings.title: H7: the Keema Pav Sliders kb-facts assertion went from an exact substring to a wildcard on the diet part
findings.scenario: If the scoped entry's diet text regresses, for example to "(non-vegetarian, vegan; Golf Course Road only)" or by losing "contains dairy", the test still passes. Only the two dessert entries are pinned exactly. None of the other diet combinations in the fixture are pinned: [] → "non-vegetarian", egg → "vegetarian; contains dairy, egg", jain → "vegan, gluten-free, Jain option available", contains-only → "non-vegetarian; contains dairy".
findings.evidence: Removed: `expect(f.get("menu-cat:small-plates")).toContain("Keema Pav Sliders ₹525 (Golf Course Road only)");`. Added: `expect(f.get("menu-cat:small-plates")).toMatch(/Keema Pav Sliders ₹525 \(non-vegetarian[^)]*; Golf Course Road only\)/);`. The actual rendered text is "Keema Pav Sliders ₹525 (non-vegetarian; contains dairy; Golf Course Road only)", which could be asserted exactly. The other changed tests are not weaker. chat-turn prompt_version v3→v4 has the same strictness. The llm-prompt v2-diff test still ends in an exact `toBe(want)`, and its `.replace` additions match the prompt.ts changes. The golden rename to prompt-v4.txt is committed with content, so toMatchFileSnapshot compares rather than creating it. The paren-aware `entries` splitter gives the same counts. chat-draft and time tests only add assertions.

findings.title: LV-REG-008 can pass without exercising the D-15 verbatim booking-sentence rule its notes say it tests
findings.scenario: The answer "Yes, Golf Course Road has a covered terrace." has no booking-state words, passes grounding, cites faq:outdoor-seating and passes the case. The booking sentence ("ask for it in the booking note and we'll try to seat you there") is never required. The case currently fails 3/3 at d9fa131 (faq_fallback, cited none), and the result files record no trace of why.
findings.evidence: Notes: "the fact's booking sentence must survive the D-15 verbatim rule". Expectation: `{"intent": "faq", "mustAbstain": false, "mustCiteAny": ["faq:outdoor-seating"]}`, with no replyMustMatch on the booking-note sentence (e.g. "booking note"). Fixture faq:outdoor-seating: "Golf Course Road has a covered terrace; ask for it in the booking note and we'll try to seat you there. Hauz Khas has indoor seating only." The expectations of the other new cases check out against the fixture: 3 Nov is inside the horizon, 25 and 30 Dec are outside it, Sat 17 Oct is "this Saturday", Gurugram Sunday lunch and dinner are open, and party sizes are within 1–8.

findings.title: Prompt v4 regresses bare-weekday dates: 'Monday night' becomes Tue 20 Oct (passes 3/3 on v3, 1/7 on v4), and the commit calls it flaky
findings.scenario: Eval now is Fri 16 Oct 2026, 14:00 IST. The guest types 'Is there a table for 2 on Monday night in Gurugram'. The v4 prompt has the Weekdays list ('Monday = 2026-10-19', 'Tuesday = 2026-10-20') and rule 2 sends a bare weekday to that list. The model returns date 2026-10-20. The bot replies 'Here are the open times for Tue 20 Oct · Golf Course Road · 2 guests.' If the guest taps a slot, the confirm card shows Tuesday instead of the Monday they asked for.
findings.evidence: This is a measured result, not a guess. The v3 baseline (evals/results/2026-10-20T09-18-11-078Z_qwen3.5-9b_baseline.json, sha 32fd853, promptVersion v3, 3 runs) passes LV-CLAIM-001 in all 3 runs, each replying 'Here are the open times for Mon 19 Oct'. Under v4 it fails in v4-try3 (Tue 20 Oct) and in 2 of the 3 claim001-repeat runs (Tue 20 Oct). In the clean-tree run at d9fa131 (evals/results/2026-10-20T10-21-07-607Z_qwen3.5-9b.json, gitDirty false, runs 3) it fails 3/3 with the failure 'draft {"branch":"gurugram","date":"2026-10-20",...} does not match {.."date":"2026-10-19"..}'. The only date-related changes in v4 are rule 2 at line 84 ('means the date given for it under "Weekdays"') and the new block at line 97: `Weekdays (the first of each after today):\n${weekdayLines(...)}`. The commit message lists this case as 'LV-CLAIM-001 flaky (1/3 runs pass: Monday read as Tuesday)'. It is really a v4 regression (v3 passed 3/3). The weekday list was only shown to work for Saturday and Sunday (LV-REG-009/010, LV-BK-001). LV-CLAIM-001 is the only D2 case with a bare Monday–Friday weekday, and it fails. Cause not isolated: confirming that the Weekdays block, rather than the rule 2 rewording, causes this needs an A/B run, which I did not run.

findings.title: Rule 1's 'confirmed booking' test cannot be applied, because the confirmation never reaches history: a change after booking starts a new booking
findings.scenario: 1. The guest books 2 at Hauz Khas tomorrow 8pm, and the confirm card POST returns 201. 2. The guest types 'actually make it Sunday instead' (or the rule's own example, 'actually make it 4 people'). 3. The model is classifying a change to a confirmed booking. Under v4 rule 1 such changes count as 'booking', and the history looks exactly like a booking still being arranged. So the model returns intent booking. 4. The code merges into the cleared draft and starts a new booking flow ('Which branch?') instead of the manage_booking template 'To change or cancel, please call {branch} on {phone}'. 5. If the guest finishes the flow with a new date or a non-overlapping time, a second reservation is saved and the original stays, holding a table the guest believes was moved. DUPLICATE_BOOKING only catches an overlap at the same branch.
findings.evidence: Rule 1 now says: '"booking" when ... changes the details of the booking being arranged in this chat ("actually make it 4 people", "make it lunch instead"); "manage_booking" only to change or cancel a booking that is already confirmed'. The model has no way to tell 'already confirmed' apart: (1) lib/chat/submit.ts:70 returns `text: "", blocks: [confirmation] ... clearDraft: true`; (2) components/chat/ChatPanel.tsx:70-74 builds history with `.filter((i) => i.id !== "welcome" && i.tone !== "error" && i.text)`, which drops the text-less confirmation item; (3) the draft and context are reset after the 201. The last assistant message the model sees is still 'Here are your booking details. Add your name and mobile number, then tap Confirm.', the same setup as LV-REG-001. Under v3 ('manage_booking to change or cancel an existing booking') the model leaned toward manage_booking for such changes; the baseline even put the in-progress LV-CONF-002 there. No D2 or D1 case covers a change typed after a successful submit.

findings.title: Today's weekday always maps to next week: 'this Saturday at 7pm' said on a Saturday lands 7 days later, and the first example teaches it
findings.scenario: 1. Today is Saturday (say 24 Oct, 14:00 IST). 2. The guest types 'book a table for 2 at Golf Course Road this Saturday at 7pm', meaning tonight. 3. Rule 2 sends the bare weekday to Weekdays, and that list starts at tomorrow, so it reads 'Saturday = 2026-10-31'. 4. On that day the first example renders the same message with date 2026-10-31. 5. The confirm card shows Sat 31 Oct. The same happens on a Friday (the eval 'now') for 'table Friday at 9pm', which gets Fri 23 Oct. 'Friday tonight' now contradicts itself, because 'tonight' means today and 'Friday' means the 23rd. Rule 3 can never treat this as ambiguous, because rule 2 makes it a lookup.
findings.evidence: calendar.ts:26-29: `horizonDates(now, zone, 7).slice(1)` drops today. prompt.ts:54-58: `nextWeekday` loops from `i = 1`, so `sat` is never today. Both feed the line-62 example 'this Saturday at 7pm' → `date: sat`. Rule 2 (line 84): 'a weekday on its own ("Sunday", "this Sunday", ...) means the date given for it under "Weekdays"'. This 'first date after today' meaning is inherited from the v2 rule (docs/MODEL_SELECTION.md:51), but v4 turns it from a rule the model could reason around into a fixed lookup. No D2 case uses the current day's weekday on its own: the eval now is Friday and no case says 'Friday' or 'this Friday'. The confirm card does show the absolute date, so the guest can catch it, which is why this is rated medium.

findings.title: The prompt quotes the failing D2 cases it was tuned to fix, so their passes measure copying, not generalisation
findings.scenario: LV-CONF-001 ('actually make it lunch instead'), LV-CONF-002 ('actually make that 4 people'), LV-BK-007 ('on the 28th') and LV-INV-004 ('on 30 December') now pass because the system prompt contains almost the same words as worked examples. They are counted as fixes in 'baseline 75/81 → v4 88/91'. If the model's handling of reworded meal or party changes, day-of-month dates, or out-of-range dates got worse, those 4 cases would keep passing and hide it. Only the single-phrasing regressions LV-REG-001..004 would show it.
findings.evidence: Rule 1 (line 83) contains '("actually make it 4 people", "make it lunch instead")'. Rule 2 (line 84) contains '("the 28th")' and '("30 December")', the last word for word from LV-INV-004 'Book Hauz Khas for 4 people on 30 December' (evals/cases/live-d2.jsonl:40), with LV-BK-007 at :25 and LV-CONF-001/002 at :63-64. §6.5 says robustness comes from writing several phrasings per category. The commit says the regression cases were reworded 'so the fix isn't tuned to one wording', yet the original wordings now sit inside the prompt.

findings.title: Rule 2's 'the next one' moves a past day and month to next year, so the guest hears the 30-day message instead of 'That date has passed'
findings.scenario: Now is Fri 16 Oct 2026. The guest types 'table for 2 at Hauz Khas on 12 October'. 12 Oct is not in the calendar (16 Oct to 15 Nov). Rule 2 says a day and month outside the calendar 'is still written as one YYYY-MM-DD date, the next one', so the model returns 2027-10-12. validateField gives past_horizon, and the guest sees 'Bookings open up to 30 days ahead. Which date would you like?' instead of pastDate, 'That date has passed.' A month-less day number missing from the window (e.g. 'the 30th' while the calendar runs 31 Jan to 2 Mar 2027) is left undefined by both new date rules.
findings.evidence: Rule 2 text: 'A day and month beyond the calendar ("30 December") is still written as one YYYY-MM-DD date, the next one, never as an ambiguity.' It does not separate dates before the calendar from dates after it. lib/chat/draft.ts:27-28 maps offset < 0 to past_date and offset > horizon to past_horizon. The messages are in lib/chat/templates.ts:33-34. No D1 or D2 case asks for a past day and month.

verdicts.title: gitSha, gitDirty and the dataset hash are read when the run ends, not when its code and cases were loaded, so a commit or edit during a background run gets attached to a run that never used it
verdicts.reasoning: I confirmed this in d9fa131:evals/run.ts. cases is loaded at the start (loadCases(casesDir), before the warm-up), and every lib/ module is imported statically when the process starts. datasetHash (fs.readdirSync + readFileSync of casesDir), gitSha (git rev-parse) and the new gitDirty (git status --porcelain) are all computed after the run loop, measureRetrieval and ollamaState, just before `const meta`. The project's own workflow makes the race plausible. MASTER_PROMPT line 468 says to run `eval` and `verify:release` in the background and poll them, and CLAUDE.md says to update docs/STATUS.md after every task. verify.ts runs `eval --runs 3` as the last step, so it takes a long time. Two concrete cases: (1) the agent edits docs/STATUS.md during the run, so a run on committed code is saved with gitDirty=true; (2) the agent commits during the run, so the result records gitSha=B, gitDirty=false and dataset.hash over B's case files, while dataset.cases and the code that actually ran are A's. The second case gives a committed results file that says B passed a release D2 run it never had, which fits the rubric's 'test weakness that would let a regression through'. The timing of gitSha and the dataset hash was already there before this commit. The new gitDirty field takes on the same timing, and its comment says it identifies 'the code that ran', which it does not in the documented background workflow. You can partly recover by comparing meta.startedAt with B's commit time, which is why I rated it medium and not higher. The 10-21-07 result (gitSha d9fa131, gitDirty false) is correct only because nothing changed during that run.
verdicts.suggestedFix: Capture the provenance once, right after loadCases() and before the warm-up: `const prov = { gitSha: sh('git',['rev-parse','--short','HEAD']), gitDirty: dirty(), datasetHash: hashCases(casesDir) }`. Use prov in meta. Optionally recompute at the end and record `treeChangedDuringRun: true` (or both snapshots) when they differ.

verdicts.title: gitDirty reports a clean tree when git fails, and the substring filter can hide changed code
verdicts.reasoning: `(sh(...) ?? "")` does turn a git failure into gitDirty=false, but none of the three scenarios can happen in this setup. (a) Running from outside the repo: `npm run eval` always runs with the package root as cwd, and verify.ts spawns with `cwd: ROOT`. Started from $HOME, tsx would find no tsconfig.json from the cwd, so the `@/lib/...` path aliases (tsconfig `paths: {"@/*": ["./*"]}`, no package.json imports map) would not resolve and the runner would crash on import long before meta is built. In any other git-failure case gitSha is also null in the same record, so it is visible that provenance is unknown. (b) A staged move of lib source into evals/results/ is not a workflow this project uses. Any real code change also shows up as a separate porcelain line that the filter does not drop. (c) `git config --get status.showUntrackedFiles` returns nothing (exit 1) on this machine, so untracked files are listed. An untracked module can only affect the run if a tracked file imports it, and that tracked file would show as modified. The 10-21-07 result correctly shows gitDirty=false next to a single `?? evals/results/...` line.
verdicts.suggestedFix: Optional hardening, not needed for correctness: pass `cwd: ROOT` in sh(), record `gitDirty: null` when git status returns null, use `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=normal`, and filter on the path (the part after the two status columns, and both sides of `->`) with startsWith('evals/results/') instead of includes().

verdicts.title: ollamaState matches models by exact name, so an untagged model reports digest null and 'not loaded' although it served every turn
verdicts.reasoning: I confirmed this in d9fa131:evals/run.ts. ollamaState's `find` compares `m.name === name || m.model === name` against config.chatModel and config.embedModel as configured. lib/config's modelName is only `z.string().min(1)` plus the cloud check, so `EMBED_MODEL=qwen3-embedding` is accepted, and Ollama resolves it to and lists it as `qwen3-embedding:latest` in /api/tags and /api/ps. The lookup then misses, and meta.ollama records digest:null and loaded:false for a model that served the run, so the §6.6 digest and §6.5 ps data are missing. The impact is narrow. Only metadata is wrong, and pass/fail and the thresholds are unaffected. scripts/model-check.ts uses the same exact-match lookup and fails with 'not pulled' on such a name, so verify:release already shows a failed model:check before this eval step. The gap is only silent in a standalone `npm run eval`. With the default names (`qwen3.5:9b`, `qwen3-embedding:0.6b`) it works: the 10-21-07 result has both digests and gpuShare 1. The re-pull-during-run variant is contrived, and I did not count it.
verdicts.suggestedFix: Normalise before matching, e.g. `const norm = (n) => (n.includes(':') ? n : `${n}:latest`).toLowerCase()`, and compare norm(m.name ?? m.model) === norm(name). Prefer the ps entry's own `digest` when the model is loaded (`(p ?? find(tags,name))?.digest`). Apply the same normalisation in scripts/model-check.ts.

verdicts.title: Clock-time guard checks the whole message for any digit or number word, so an invented time still gets through whenever a party size or date is in the same message
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed in d9fa131. CLOCK_RE (lib/chat/draft.ts:117) is `/\p{Nd}|\b(?:noon|...|one|two|...|twelve)\b/iu`, so statesClockTime only asks whether the message contains any digit or number word anywhere. The guard in turn.ts:209 drops booking.time only when that test is false. I traced "actually make it lunch for 2 instead" on the SC-REG-006 draft (hauz-khas, 2026-10-17, 20:00, dinner, 4) with the model inventing 12:00, the same mistake it made in v4-try1 LV-CONF-001. The "2" matches, so the time is kept. mergeExtracted sets time=12:00, timeWindow=lunch and partySize=2, then calls latestWins(statedTime = booking.time !== null = true), so the time is not cleared. withSelection only clears `selected`. nextStep then reaches availabilityStep, which finds the exact 12:00 slot (router.ts:165-168) and returns a confirm card for 12:00 PM. "Can I book for two this Sunday evening at the Gurugram one?" also passes the test, through both "two" and "one". Prompt v4 rule 2 asks the model not to do this, but v4-try1 showed it still can, and SC-REG-006, which the project rates critical, exists because of that. The commit does not make things worse than before (previously no time was ever dropped), but its stated protection only works for number-free messages. Most real booking messages contain a party size or a date, so the original failure (an invented time on a confirm card that looks like a normal lunch time) stays open. Under the rubric that is high: wrong booking details reach a confirm card. It depends on the model making the mistake, so it is not critical.
verdicts.suggestedFix: Check that the model's time is supported by the message, not just that the message has a number. Build a set of hours from the masked message: 1-2 digit runs, number words with an optional suffix (`\b(one|...|twelve)(?:-?ish)?\b`, plus nineteen/twenty...), noon/midday → 12 and midnight → 0. In turn.ts, drop booking.time unless its hour h, or h-12, is in that set. Alternatively, require a time context next to the number (am/pm, ':', '.', o'clock, at/around/by, half/quarter, -ish). Add tests where the guard must drop the time: "make it lunch for 2 instead" → 12:00, and "for two this Sunday evening at the Gurugram one" → 19:00. Add a scripted regression variant of SC-REG-006 that includes a party size.

verdicts.title: A real time is dropped when written as a number word with a suffix ('nineish', 'eightish') or as 'nineteen hundred'; the old time's confirm card then comes back as if the change worked
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed, and this commit introduced it. In JS, `\bnine\b` cannot match inside "nineish" because there is no word boundary between 'e' and 'i'. Nothing else matches in "can we do nineish instead?": no digit, and no standalone number word or noon/half/quarter. "nineteen hundred" fails the same way ('nine' is followed by 't', and "teen" is not "ten"). "nine-ish" and "9ish" do match. Path: the draft is hauz-khas, 2026-10-17, 20:00, timeWindow null, 4, with a selection. The model returns time 21:00 and everything else null. turn.ts:209 drops it, so booking.time is null. In mergeExtracted every field is null, so nothing changes. latestWins(statedTime=false) does nothing because the window did not change. withSelection keeps the selection. nextStep then calls availabilityStep with time 20:00, which finds the exact slot (router.ts:165) and shows the 8:00 PM confirm card with "Here are your booking details... tap Confirm". Before this commit, 21:00 would have gone through. The card states 8:00 PM, which contradicts the guest's request, so the mistake is visible and the guest can fix it. Only the joined-up word forms are affected. That makes it medium, not high.
verdicts.suggestedFix: The same support-check as finding 1 fixes this: match number words with an optional '-?ish' suffix and the compound forms (nineteen, twenty, 'hundred'), and keep the model time when its hour matches. Add positive unit cases "nineish", "eightish", "nineteen hundred" and "sevenish please".

verdicts.title: When exactly one ambiguity reading is usable, the older draft value is kept and its confirm card is shown again; the new comment says the flow 'asks plainly', which is only true for an empty field
verdicts.reasoning: The code does this as committed, but the behaviour predates this commit, which only added the comment (draft.ts:84-85) and an empty-draft test (chat-draft.test.ts:74). Path: the draft is party 4, 20:00 tomorrow, with a confirm card showing. The model follows prompt rule 3 for "8 or 9 of us" and returns partySize null with ambiguity ["8","9"]. validateField rejects "9" as large_party (onlinePartyMax 8), so candidates is ["8"]. ambiguity stays null, and unusable stays null because candidates.length is 1. The loop skips the null partySize, so nothing is rejected or changed, and withSelection keeps the selection. nextStep has no ambiguity, large party or issue to act on, so it goes to availabilityStep with party 4, finds the exact 20:00 slot and shows the 4-guest confirm card again. That breaks §5.7 ('the latest stated value wins', 'if one message contradicts itself, ask'). The new comment ('asks plainly') is only true when the draft field was empty. The card states 4 guests, so the guest can see and fix it. That makes it medium.
verdicts.suggestedFix: In mergeExtracted, when an ambiguity has exactly one usable candidate for branch, date or partySize, add the field to `rejected` so latestWins clears it and nextStep asks for it. For partySize, also set largeParty if any candidate is large_party. Add a unit test with a pre-filled draft (partySize 4, candidates ["8","9"]) that expects draft.partySize null or largeParty, not an unchanged draft.

verdicts.title: Tests for both guards only cover number-free messages and empty drafts, so the gaps above would go unnoticed
verdicts.reasoning: The claim is accurate. The statesClockTime negatives (chat-draft.test.ts:90) are all number-free. SC-REG-006 uses the number-free message. The new ambiguity test uses draft({}). LV-BK-001, LV-BK-009 and LV-REG-009 check draft fields through a partial deepMatch (evals/run.ts:88-92) with no time:null and no noActions:["confirm"]. No invariant checks for an unstated time (INV-03 only checks that offered starts are open). So an invented time on a confirm card would pass every current test and eval. This is the test side of findings 1 to 3, though, not a separate defect: number-bearing negatives cannot be added without first fixing finding 1. Rated low because adding the regression tests should be part of the fixes for findings 1 to 3.
verdicts.suggestedFix: Add the tests together with the fixes for findings 1 to 3: number-bearing negatives for the guard ('lunch for 2 instead' → 12:00 dropped), '-ish' positives, a scripted SC-REG-006 variant with a party size, and time:null plus noActions:["confirm"] on LV-BK-001, LV-BK-009 and LV-REG-009.

verdicts.title: The unusable-ambiguity reason comes from whichever candidate is listed first, so the guest can be given the wrong reason
verdicts.reasoning: The code does this: `const first = checked[0]` (draft.ts:86) takes the issue from the first listed candidate with no ranking. With candidates ["2025-12-30","2026-12-30"] on 16 Oct 2026, that is past_date, and ISSUE_TEXT maps it to "That date has passed." when the useful reason is the 30-day limit. With ["0","12"], bad_party gives a plain "How many guests?" instead of the large-party phone template. The trigger is unlikely, though. Prompt v4 rule 2 tells the model to write a day and month beyond the calendar as one upcoming date, never as an ambiguity. The prompt only gives dates from today onward. In every recorded LV-INV-004 run, the reply was either the generic ask or the 30-day message, never 'has passed'. The guest still gets a question about the right field, so the only harm is a misleading reason.
verdicts.suggestedFix: Choose the reason by priority rather than position, for example `const RANK: FieldIssue[] = ["large_party","past_horizon","branch_inactive","past_date","bad_party","bad_date","bad_branch","bad_time"]; const issue = RANK.find((r) => checked.some((c) => !c.ok && c.issue === r));`.

verdicts.title: The not-stated guard only drops booking.time; a time ambiguity from a message with no time still produces time chips
verdicts.reasoning: The code does this. turn.ts:209-211 checks and clears only turn.booking.time and leaves booking.ambiguity alone. If the model returns ambiguity {time, ["12:00","13:00"]} for "make it lunch instead", mergeExtracted validates both times (format only), builds the ambiguity, and nextStep returns "Which time did you mean?" with 12:00 PM and 1:00 PM chips (router.ts:115-119). The harm is small. Prompt rule 3 tells the model a field the guest did not mention is never ambiguous. Time field chips are not offered slots: offeredStarts only checks slots and confirm blocks. Nothing reaches a confirm card unless the guest taps a chip, and that tap goes through applySetField to availabilityStep, which checks the engine. The result is a confusing question, not wrong details on a card the guest did not choose.
verdicts.suggestedFix: In turn.ts, apply the same check to the ambiguity: if turn.booking.ambiguity?.field === "time" and the message states no clock time (using the fixed check from finding 1), set booking.ambiguity to null and push an ignore_field trace entry.

verdicts.title: Category lists label vegan dishes only as "vegan"; with v4 rule 4, answers to "which X are vegetarian" now drop every vegan dish
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed in code and in the committed results. dietText (lib/kb/facts.ts:107) picks one base label, so a vegan item never carries the word "vegetarian". The new diet(m) entry renders menu-cat:small-plates as "Kale Pakoda ₹295 (vegan, gluten-free)" and "Beetroot & Peanut Tikki ₹345 (vegan, gluten-free; contains nuts)". v4 rule 4 tells the model to call a dish vegetarian only if the facts say so. Fixture tags: kale-pakoda [vegan, gluten-free], beetroot-peanut-tikki [vegan, gluten-free, contains-nuts]. In the d9fa131 run (2026-10-20T10-21-07-607Z, gitSha d9fa131, gitDirty false), LV-REG-005 shows "The vegetarian small plates are Papdi Chaat (₹315), Dahi Puri Shots (₹325), and Mushroom Galouti (₹425)." in all 3 runs, citing menu-cat:small-plates and three per-item facts. v4-try1, try2 and try3 give the same omission. The pre-v4 run listed all five. The answer is presented as the complete list, so it wrongly says the two vegan plates are not vegetarian. Grounding cannot catch this because no number or booking word changes. The omission is the safe direction (no meat dish is called vegetarian), but a wrong menu fact reaches the guest every time.
verdicts.suggestedFix: Make the label state that vegan items are also vegetarian. For example, have dietText return "Vegan (also vegetarian)", or have diet() emit "vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free" for vegan items. Apply it to both menu-cat entries and per-item menu facts. Then add positive checks to LV-REG-005 (see the LV-REG-005/006 finding).

verdicts.title: statesClockTime treats any digit or number word as a clock time, so party sizes and dates let an invented time through to a confirm card
verdicts.reasoning: The code hole is confirmed. CLOCK_RE (lib/chat/draft.ts:117) is /\p{Nd}|\b(?:noon|...|one|two|...|twelve)\b/iu, so "actually make it lunch for 4 instead", "lunch on the 18th instead" and "for four this Saturday night" all return true. The turn.ts:209 guard then keeps the model's time. mergeExtracted passes statedTime=true to latestWins, so the old-time-clearing branch is skipped and the draft gets time 12:00. Committed v4-try1 shows the downstream result for this exact model error: LV-CONF-001 produced 'confirm hauz-khas 2026-10-17 12:00 x4', a time the guest never gave. The d9fa131 run offers 12:00 for 4 at Hauz Khas on Sat lunch, so the slot is open. The unit tests' false cases are all digit-free, and SC-REG-006 only covers the digit-free phrasing. Rated medium, not high: it needs the model to invent a time, which I could not reproduce for the digit-bearing phrasing in a read-only review. It is not a regression, since 6cfa174 had no guard at all. The guest also sees the time on the card before entering details and confirming, so any saved row matches what was shown.
verdicts.suggestedFix: Match clock times, not bare numbers. For example: /\b\d{1,2}(?::\d{2})?\s*(?:am|pm|a\.m\.|p\.m\.|o'?clock|hrs?)\b|\b\d{1,2}:\d{2}\b|\b(?:at|around|by|from|after|before)\s+(?:\d{1,2}|one|two|...|twelve)\b|\b(?:noon|midday|midnight)\b|\b(?:half|quarter)\s+(?:past|to)\b/iu. Fullwidth digits need the \p{Nd} form or normalization. Add false cases such as "make it lunch for 4 instead", "lunch on the 18th instead" and "for four this Saturday night", plus a scripted case like SC-REG-006 with a digit in the message. LV-CONF-002 still works because null never clears the draft's 20:00.

verdicts.title: LV-REG-005/006 check only for forbidden dish names, so wrong or incomplete diet answers pass and count as grounded-correct
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed. In the d9fa131 run, LV-REG-005 passed in all 3 runs with the incomplete answer from the first finding. Its checks are intent, answer (not abstained) and four replyMustNotMatch patterns. evals/run.ts:147 records the 'answer' key, and evals/metrics.ts:31 puts 'answer' in GROUNDED_KEYS, so the wrong answer raises groundedAnswerCorrectness. With no positive dish check, a reply like "None of our drinks are vegan" would also pass LV-REG-006. Patterns use new RegExp(re, "i") (run.ts:150), so a correct answer that names the excluded drinks ("...the lassi, chaas, coffee and chai contain dairy") would fail. The case it rephrases, LV-SMOKE-04, has a replyMustMatch plus mustIncludeValues; these do not. This is a test weakness that already let a real regression through.
verdicts.suggestedFix: LV-REG-005: add replyMustMatch ["Kale Pakoda", "Beetroot", "Papdi Chaat", "Dahi Puri", "Mushroom Galouti"] and mustCiteAny ["menu-cat:small-plates", "menu-diet:vegetarian"]. LV-REG-006: add replyMustMatch ["Kokum Cooler", "Fresh Lime Soda"]. Optionally anchor the negative patterns to a claim, for example /(Lassi|Chaas|Coffee|Chai)[^.]*\bvegan\b/, so a correct contrasting answer passes.

verdicts.title: LV-REG-009 does not require time:null, so an invented "night" time would pass (the guard is bypassed by "four")
verdicts.reasoning: The mechanics are confirmed. deepMatch (evals/run.ts:88-92) is a subset match, and LV-REG-009's draft expectation omits time and has no noActions confirm. "four" matches CLOCK_RE, so an invented 20:00 would be kept, a confirm card would be shown, and the case would still pass and count as 'all fields exact'. Current runs pass for the right reason (slots shown, time null). Rated low: the case is a weekday probe whose purpose is the date, and many older booking cases share the pattern (LV-BK-001/002/009/010, LV-REG-003). An invented-time regression would still be caught elsewhere: LV-SLOT-002 expects a slots block, and the LV-AMB cases use noActions ["confirm"]. The underlying hole is the statesClockTime finding.
verdicts.suggestedFix: Add "time": null to LV-REG-009's expect.draft and "noActions": ["confirm"]. Do the same for LV-REG-003, which has a meal word, digits and no clock time.

verdicts.title: H7: the Keema Pav Sliders kb-facts assertion went from an exact substring to a wildcard on the diet part
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed. The old assertion was an exact toContain. The new one, /Keema Pav Sliders ₹525 \(non-vegetarian[^)]*; Golf Course Road only\)/, would still pass if the scoped entry lost "; contains dairy". The real rendered string is exactly "Keema Pav Sliders ₹525 (non-vegetarian; contains dairy; Golf Course Road only)" (dietText(["contains-dairy"]) → "Non-vegetarian; contains dairy." → lowercased, period stripped). It could have been pinned. tests/golden/prompt-v4.txt has no menu-cat lines, so no snapshot backs it up. The wildcard cannot admit "non-vegetarian, vegan" because dietText emits one base label. Minor looseness on one assertion.
verdicts.suggestedFix: Replace the regex with expect(f.get("menu-cat:small-plates")).toContain("Keema Pav Sliders ₹525 (non-vegetarian; contains dairy; Golf Course Road only)"). Optionally pin one egg entry (Chocolate Chilli Mousse ₹345 (vegetarian; contains dairy, egg)) and one Jain entry.

verdicts.title: LV-REG-008 can pass without exercising the D-15 verbatim booking-sentence rule its notes say it tests
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed. The expectation is only {intent faq, mustAbstain false, mustCiteAny [faq:outdoor-seating]}. A reply like "Yes, Golf Course Road has a covered terrace." has none of the claims.ts booking-state words (book*, reserv*, confirm*, table, seat, ...), passes grounding, and cites the fact. It would pass without the booking-note sentence that the notes say must survive D-15. In the d9fa131 run the case fails 3/3 (faq_fallback, cited none). The result turns carry no trace, so the cause is not recorded. That is a reporting gap, not a wrong result. Low: the case cannot pass on a wrong answer, but it may not test what it claims to.
verdicts.suggestedFix: Add replyMustMatch ["booking note"] (and optionally ["covered terrace"]) so the case requires the verbatim booking sentence. Optionally record the routing trace, or at least the fallback reason, in the result turns so a fallback can be diagnosed.

verdicts.title: Prompt v4 regresses bare-weekday dates: 'Monday night' becomes Tue 20 Oct (passes 3/3 on v3, 1/7 on v4), and the commit calls it flaky
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed from the committed result files with jq. v3 baseline (32fd853, promptVersion v3, 3 runs): LV-CLAIM-001 passes 3/3, each reply 'Here are the open times for Mon 19 Oct · Golf Course Road · 2 guests.' v4: v4-try3 fails (date 2026-10-20), claim001-repeat passes 1/3 (2 runs give 2026-10-20), and the clean run at d9fa131 (2026-10-20T10-21-07-607Z, gitDirty false, runs 3) fails 3/3 with draft date 2026-10-20 and reply 'Here are the open times for Tue 20 Oct'. No post-model code changes the date. statesClockTime only drops time, and mergeExtracted only adds the 'unusable ambiguity' path. So the wrong date comes from the model under the committed prompt. The golden prompt-v4.txt shows the Weekdays block is correct ('Monday = 2026-10-19', 'Tuesday = 2026-10-20'), so the model is misreading the new lookup or the reworded rule 2, not getting bad data. The wrong date reaches the slots reply, and from a slot tap it reaches the confirm card, which matches the 'high' rubric. The commit message calls this 'flaky (1/3 runs pass)', but it is a reproducible regression against a 3/3 v3 pass. One part of the evidence is wrong: LV-CLAIM-001 is not the only bare Mon–Fri case. LV-BK-003 ('on Wednesday' → 2026-10-21) and LV-BK-005 ('on thursday') exist and pass in the clean run. So the regression is narrower (Monday, maybe with 'night') than 'bare weekdays', but it is real. The cause (Weekdays block vs rule 2 wording) is not isolated.
verdicts.suggestedFix: Treat it as a regression, not flakiness. Record it in STATUS/EVAL_REPORT as 'fails 3/3 at d9fa131, passed 3/3 on v3'. Run a one-case A/B with the v3 rule 2 weekday sentence and the Weekdays block, then without the block. A likely minimal fix is to label the Weekdays lines like the calendar ('Monday = Mon 19 Oct = 2026-10-19'), or to drop the separate block and mark weekday rows inside the calendar. Add regression cases for bare 'Monday', 'Tuesday' and 'Friday' (with and without 'night') before changing the prompt (§6.6).

verdicts.title: Rule 1's 'confirmed booking' test cannot be applied, because the confirmation never reaches history: a change after booking starts a new booking
verdicts.reasoning: The code path checks out. submitOutcome returns text '' with only a confirmation block (lib/chat/submit.ts:70). ChatPanel's history() filters out items with empty text (components/chat/ChatPanel.tsx:72), so the confirmation is dropped. post() then sets the draft to null and the context to {lastCitedIds: []} (lines 159-160), and the context schema carries only lastCitedIds. So for a typed change after a 201, the model sees the same history as LV-REG-001/LV-CONF-002: a guest booking line, then the assistant confirmIntro 'Here are your booking details... tap Confirm.' The only difference is an all-null draft, and rule 2 tells the model never to use the draft. v4 rule 1 says changes to 'the booking being arranged in this chat' are booking, and the rule's own example is 'actually make it 4 people'. The model therefore has no input that separates 'already confirmed'. The measured v4 passes of LV-REG-001/002 on this exact history shape show it returns booking there. v3 sent the same shape to manage_booking (the baseline LV-CONF-001/002 failures), which happened to be correct after a confirmation. With booking, the router merges into the empty draft and asks for the branch instead of giving the T.manageBooking 'please call' redirect. A party-only change at the same slot is caught later by DUPLICATE_BOOKING (same branch, overlapping, same phone). A date or branch change completes as a second saved reservation while the original stays. No D1/D2 case types a guest message after a submit (LV-BOOK-001, LV-DUP-001/002, LV-SMOKE-02 and LV-CTX-001 all end at SUBMIT). The model output for this exact post-confirm input is predicted, not measured. The guest also sees the flow restart and gets a new ref, so the behaviour is visible and recoverable. That makes it medium, not higher.
verdicts.suggestedFix: Give the model an observable signal. After a 201, add a non-empty assistant history line (e.g. 'Booking confirmed (ref X).') or a context flag such as lastConfirmedRef, which the server turns into a history or user-prompt line. Alternatively, route deterministically: if the draft is empty, the previous turn was a confirmation, and the model says booking with a change phrase, use manage_booking. Add a D1 and a D2 case: submit 201, then 'actually make it Sunday instead', expecting a manage_redirect outcome and 0 extra rows.

verdicts.title: Today's weekday always maps to next week: 'this Saturday at 7pm' said on a Saturday lands 7 days later, and the first example teaches it
verdicts.reasoning: The mechanics are right: weekdayLines uses horizonDates(...,7).slice(1) (calendar.ts:27-28), and examplesText's nextWeekday starts at i = 1 (prompt.ts:55), so today's weekday maps to +7. But this is the documented, approved semantics carried over from prompt v2 ('A weekday means the first calendar date after today with that weekday', docs/MODEL_SELECTION.md:51), and v3 rule 2 said exactly that ('the first calendar date after today with that weekday'). examplesText is unchanged by d9fa131, so the 'this Saturday' example already behaved this way under v3. d9fa131 encodes the existing rule as a lookup and does not change any outcome the rule defines. The 'model could reason around it' argument is speculation. Whether 'this Saturday' said on a Saturday means tonight is a product-spec question, not a defect introduced here. The confirm card shows the absolute date, as the finding itself notes.
verdicts.suggestedFix: No change needed for this commit. If the product wants it, make 'this <today's weekday>' an ambiguity (candidates today and +7) via rule 3, and add a D2 case with a Saturday 'now'. Treat that as a spec decision under DECISIONS.md, not a v4 fix.

verdicts.title: The prompt quotes the failing D2 cases it was tuned to fix, so their passes measure copying, not generalisation
verdicts.reasoning: It is true that rule 1/2 contain near-verbatim wordings of LV-CONF-002 ('actually make that 4 people'), LV-CONF-001 ('actually make it lunch instead'), LV-BK-007 ('the 28th') and LV-INV-004 ('30 December'). But the failure scenario, a regression hidden from the suite, does not happen. Each contaminated case has an uncontaminated sibling added in this commit, with wordings not in the prompt: LV-REG-001 'oh wait, can we make it 5 of us instead?', LV-REG-002 'can we switch to dinner instead?', LV-REG-003 'the 3rd', LV-REG-004 '25 December'. A drop in handling reworded inputs would fail those cases and the D2 run, as the finding itself concedes. So no regression slips through. What remains is a small inflation of the '88/91' headline, which is a reporting issue for the not-yet-written EVAL_REPORT, not a code defect.
verdicts.suggestedFix: Optional: in EVAL_REPORT, mark LV-CONF-001/002, LV-BK-007 and LV-INV-004 as prompt-contaminated and report generalisation from LV-REG-001..004. Or change the in-prompt examples to wordings that appear in no case (e.g. 'change it to 6 of us', 'the 5th', '2 January').

verdicts.title: Rule 2's 'the next one' moves a past day and month to next year, so the guest hears the 30-day message instead of 'That date has passed'
verdicts.reasoning: The code side is right: validateField maps offset > horizon to past_horizon and offset < 0 to past_date (draft.ts:27-28), and the templates differ. But the scenario depends on unmeasured model behaviour, and the rule text doesn't clearly produce it. Rule 2 applies 'the next one' to 'a day and month beyond the calendar', and 12 October (before 16 Oct) is not naturally 'beyond' a calendar that runs forward from today. The model could as plausibly return 2026-10-12, which gives past_date. No run shows this. If an ambiguity [2026-10-12, 2027-10-12] came back, the new mergeExtracted 'unusable' path uses the first candidate's issue (past_date). Even in the worst case, the guest gets a true message ('Bookings open up to 30 days ahead. Which date would you like?') and is asked again. No booking moves forward and no wrong detail reaches a card. The 'the 30th' window case is likewise hypothetical, and an impossible date is caught as bad_date or past_horizon.
verdicts.suggestedFix: Optional: add a D2 case ('table for 2 on 12 October' at the eval now) expecting 'That date has passed'. If it fails, narrow the rule to 'a day and month after the calendar's last date', or say a day and month already passed this year is written in the current year.

resolution: Fixed with regression tests before T-20 closed: see docs/EVAL_REPORT.md 'Review of the T-20 changes' and DECISIONS D-15 amendment, D-17.
